briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. We will now begin the climate briefing for August 2, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis and Major Warnings
sections.content: On the first day of August 2026, severe impacts of climate change are being reported in various regions worldwide, including South Korea. Domestically, a tropical night advisory was issued for most parts of the country on August 1st, leading to sleepless nights [13]. Internationally, rivers in the western United States are being closed for fishing by about half in August [15], and in Minnesota, severe weather conditions occurred in July, with climate change identified as the cause [20]. Particularly in Europe, climate change caused by human activities has significantly increased the likelihood of wildfires in Spain and France [17], with wildfires erupting across Europe, burning down regions [21], and even places like 'Le Camping' are threatened to turn into ashes [22]. These phenomena come with a warning that climate change is being ignored despite leading to our destruction [24], and in the Arctic region, it is even exacerbating nuclear risks, suggesting that we are unprepared [25].

sections.title: ⚠️ Increased Community Vulnerability and Biodiversity Loss
sections.content: Climate change poses a direct threat to key industries and ecosystems in specific regions. Domestically, Jeju agriculture is on the front lines of the climate crisis, and there have been calls for the urgent establishment of a comprehensive climate disaster response system [3]. Furthermore, the global wine industry is facing an existential threat due to climate change, and is exploring countermeasures such as changing grape varieties and reducing production volumes [1]. Amidst this crisis, the deep interconnectedness between biodiversity loss and the climate crisis is once again emphasized [5], demonstrating the deepening vulnerability of ecosystems across the board.

sections.title: 🌱 Efforts Towards Carbon Neutrality and Positive Progress
sections.content: Despite these critical circumstances, various efforts and positive progress towards a carbon-neutral society are being reported. Domestically, Gwangmyeong City is leading carbon-neutral practices in daily life through its 'Climate Militia' initiative [8], and Suwon City is encouraging citizen participation by operating the 'Carbon-Neutral Dream Playground Connected by Culture' [10]. At the government level, the 'National AX Project' is scheduled to officially launch in 2026, with the creation of a 'Carbon-Neutral AGI Campus' in the Seoul Metropolitan Area, expected to serve as a driving force for the future economy [11]. Internationally, Korea Zinc is actively seeking solutions through inter-state cooperation, such as proposing integrated cooperation on critical minerals and green energy to Chile, exploring 'carbon-neutral partnerships' [12]. These efforts provide reasons for hope in the face of climate change [18], demonstrating that steps towards a sustainable future are continuing even amidst the crisis.

sections.title: 📰 Challenges in Climate Change Response and Social Awareness
sections.content: As the threat of climate change grows, challenges and issues of social awareness still persist. It has been pointed out that some factors causing climate change remain unclear and hidden [16], suggesting the need for a multifaceted approach. Furthermore, political divisions regarding climate change were addressed in an op-ed [19], and in the United States, despite extreme weather events this summer, reports indicate that the climate crisis has largely disappeared from the political agenda [27]. This phenomenon, where climate change is being ignored despite leading to our destruction [24], underscores the need for continuous attention and agenda-setting efforts from the public and policymakers.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlighted the warnings of a deepening global climate crisis, along with various domestic and international efforts and challenges to address it. Only sustained attention and action will pave the way for a sustainable future. This concludes today's climate briefing.
